sessions.title: Back-Safe Gym Strength & Extended Hip Mobility
sessions.description: Progression from your 22 October gym session, with zero plyometrics or pole vaulting. 1) Warm-up: 8 minutes easy indoor rowing focusing on technique (damper 3–4, stroke rate 18–20 spm, drive with legs first, hinge at hips, keep HR <130 bpm). 2) Goblet Squats: 1x10 at 4 kg warm-up, then 3x10 at 12 kg (adding the 3rd set you skipped last week; rest 90s between sets). 3) Light Dumbbell Romanian Deadlifts (RDLs): 2x10 with light dumbbells (8–10 kg per hand), focusing strictly on pushing the hips straight back with soft knees and a flat neutral spine—stop the descent the moment your hamstrings tighten, well before any lower-back rounding. 4) Supine Glute Bridges: 3x12 with a 2-second squeeze at the top. 5) Lat Pulldowns: 3x10 at 45–50 kg. 6) Core Anti-Rotation & Stability: Pallof Press 3x10 per side + Front Plank 3x30 seconds (rest 45s between bouts). 7) Dedicated Hip & Back Flexibility (12 minutes mandatory—2.5 minutes is not enough): 90/90 hip switches, kneeling hip-flexor stretch (2 min/side), elevated-surface straight-leg hamstring hinge stretch (2 min/side), and supine figure-4 piriformis stretch.

sessions.title: Beginner Run/Walk Progression (HR Capped)
sessions.description: Easy 40-minute outdoor run/walk (bring your headlamp if running after sunset). Unlike your 22 September run where HR sat at 150–165 bpm, today's rule is strict heart-rate control: keep HR between 120 and 135 bpm from the very first minute. Start with a 5-minute brisk walk, then alternate 3 minutes of easy jogging with 2 minutes of brisk walking for 30 minutes (6 rounds), and finish with a 5-minute cool-down walk. If HR touches 135 bpm during any jog segment, transition immediately to walking until it drops below 122 bpm.

sessions.title: Rest & Evening Routine Focus
sessions.description: Scheduled rest day to shed weekday fatigue ahead of the weekend. Focus on your nutrition habit goal: prepare a high-volume, vegetable- and protein-heavy dinner so you feel full after work, and keep snacks out of reach in the kitchen before bedtime.

sessions.title: Hip Mobility, Core Activation & Pre-Hike Prep
sessions.description: Short, restorative 25-minute indoor mobility and core activation session so your legs remain completely fresh for tomorrow's 5-hour mountain hike. Pack your hiking gear and pre-portioned trail food tonight.

sessions.title: 5-Hour Mountain Hike Durability Anchor
sessions.description: The primary endurance anchor of Week 1: a 5-hour mountain hike focused on continuous aerobic durability and stop management. On your 26 September and 25 October hikes, stationary pauses ate up 20–50+ minutes and steep pitches pushed your HR to 164 bpm. Today's execution rules: 1) Keep heart rate in the 110–135 bpm band throughout—shorten your stride immediately on steeper climbs so HR never exceeds 135 bpm. 2) Cap every single break at 5 minutes maximum (set a timer when you stop) so your moving time stays high and steady. 3) Fuel lightly with 20–30 g of carbohydrates per hour during the second half so you do not return home ravenously hungry.

sessions.title: Rest Day & Evening Nutrition Focus
sessions.description: Full rest day to set up a clean, consistent week of training. Focus on your evening nutrition habit: have a planned, protein-and-vegetable-rich dinner ready after work so you don't get overly hungry, and clear visible snacks from the kitchen counter. Optional 10 minutes of gentle hip flexor and hamstring stretching before bed.

sessions.title: Back-Safe Gym Strength, Beginner Rowing & Hip Mobility
sessions.description:
Since last week's gym session was cut short at 21 minutes, today is about completing the full routine calmly with strict form.

1. Beginner Rowing Technique Warm-up (15 min): Set damper to 3–4. Focus on sequence: Legs -> Body -> Arms on the drive, then Arms -> Body -> Legs on the recovery. Row 3 x 4 minutes at 18–20 strokes per minute (spm) with 1 minute easy rest between bouts. Keep heart rate under 130 bpm.

2. Strength Circuit (30 min): Rest 60–90s between sets. Stop immediately if you feel any lower-back twinge.
- Goblet Squat: 1 warm-up set of 10 reps at 4–6 kg, then 3 x 10 reps at 12 kg (upright torso, knees tracking toes).
- Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift (RDL): 3 x 10 reps with light dumbbells (8–10 kg per hand). Keep a slight knee bend, brace your core, and hinge strictly at the hips until you feel a mild hamstring stretch (mid-shin height)—never round the lower back.
- Glute Bridges: 3 x 12 reps with a 2-second squeeze at the top.
- Lat Pulldown: 3 x 10 reps at 40–50 kg (controlled return).
- Pallof Press (Anti-Rotation Core): 3 x 10 reps per side with a 2-second hold at full extension.
- Front Plank: 3 x 30 seconds (focus on glute squeeze and ribs down).

3. Dedicated Hip & Hamstring Mobility (10 min): Do not skip this—2.5 minutes isn't enough to relieve sit-bone pressure on the bike. Do 2 rounds of: Couch stretch or half-kneeling hip flexor stretch (60s/side), 90/90 hip switches (60s), and supine hamstring strap/towel stretch with a flat lower back (60s/side).

sessions.title: Steady Zone 2 Indoor ERG Ride
sessions.description: 60 minutes on the indoor trainer in ERG mode. Goal: a completely flat, steady aerobic effort with cadence at 85–95 rpm and heart rate capped under 145 bpm. Warm up for 10 minutes building from 99 W to 121 W, hold a steady 143 W for 40 minutes, and cool down for 10 minutes at 99 W. If your legs feel heavy from Tuesday's squats and HR drifts near 145 bpm, drop the ERG target by 5–10 W. Smooth, low-stress Zone 2 work stimulates fat oxidation without triggering intense post-workout hunger.

sessions.title: Beginner Run/Walk Progression (HR Capped)
sessions.description:
40 minutes outdoors (bring your headlamp if running after work). Because your previous run in September drifted to 150–167 bpm and you haven't logged a run in several weeks, strict heart rate control is the number one rule today.

- Warm-up: 5 minutes brisk walk.
- Main Set: 6 rounds of [3 minutes easy slow jog + 2 minutes brisk walk] (30 minutes total).
- Cool-down: 5 minutes easy walk.

Keep heart rate strictly between 120 and 135 bpm. The moment HR touches 136 bpm, switch to walking even if the 3-minute jog interval isn't finished. Short, soft strides to protect your lower back and joints.

sessions.title: Back-Safe Gym Strength, Beginner Rowing & Hip Mobility B
sessions.description:
Second full-body gym and rowing session of the week to build structural resilience for long climbs and carpentry/crouching work.

1. Beginner Rowing Technique (15 min): Damper 3–4. Row 5 minutes steady at 18 spm, 2 minutes rest, then 5 minutes at 20 spm focusing on a strong leg drive and relaxed shoulders/grip, followed by 3 minutes easy cool-down. Cap HR at 130–135 bpm.

2. Strength Circuit (30 min): Rest 60–90s between sets.
- Goblet Squat: 3 x 10 reps at 12 kg (focus on depth without your lower back tucking under).
- Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift (RDL): 3 x 10 reps at 8–10 kg per hand (strict hip hinge, feel the hamstrings load, keep lats engaged).
- Bird-Dog (Back Stabilization): 3 x 8 reps per side with a 3-second hold at extension, no lumbar arching.
- Seated Cable Row or Chest-Supported Row: 3 x 10–12 reps at a moderate weight (35–45 kg), squeezing shoulder blades together.
- Suitcase Carry (Anti-Lateral Flexion Core): 3 x 30 meters per hand with a 12–16 kg kettlebell or dumbbell, walking tall without leaning.

3. Extended Hip & Back Mobility (10 min): 2 rounds of: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch (60s/side), figure-4 glute stretch on your back (60s/side), and elevated-hands hamstring hinge stretch (60s).

sessions.title: Steady Zone 2 ERG Ride (or Dry Outdoor Spin)
sessions.description: 60 minutes on the indoor trainer in ERG mode (or outdoors on your road/gravel bike with power meter if the weather is dry and you prefer fresh air). Warm up for 10 minutes from 99 W to 121 W, then hold a flat 147 W (67% FTP) for 40 minutes at 85–95 rpm, and cool down for 10 minutes at 99 W. Keep heart rate under 145 bpm throughout.

sessions.title: Weekend Mountain Hike (Stop-Capped Endurance)
sessions.description: 2.5-hour steady mountain hike (or studded-tire fatbike ride if early snow/ice has arrived and you prefer riding). Focus on the key habit from your earlier hikes: keep your moving pace steady, use short steps on steep pitches to keep heart rate between 110 and 135 bpm (avoiding surges above 150 bpm), and cap any stationary break at 5 minutes maximum so you maintain continuous aerobic stimulus and fat oxidation. Pack a light, planned snack so you arrive home satisfied and in control of Sunday dinner.

week.rationale: Last week was very light on recorded volume—only a 21-minute strength session on Tuesday was logged, with the planned ERG ride, run/walk, and Sunday hike not recorded. Rather than trying to 'make up' missed hours, we hold estimated FTP steady at 220 W and focus on re-establishing consistent daily habits this week. Because Sunday's 5-hour hike was not logged, your legs are fresh, allowing us to start the week smoothly while still keeping Monday as a full rest and nutrition-reset day. Tuesday and Friday deliver the full 55-minute back-safe gym routine (adding the 3rd goblet squat set at 12 kg, light strict-hinge RDLs, and 10+ minutes of dedicated hip mobility) paired with a 15-minute beginner indoor rowing technique progression. Wednesday and Saturday provide flat, surge-free 60-minute ERG rides at 143–147 W (65–67% FTP, HR <145 bpm) to build aerobic smoothness without triggering evening hunger spikes. Thursday re-introduces the 40-minute easy run/walk strictly capped at 125–135 bpm, and Sunday anchors the week with a steady 2.5-hour mountain hike.

today.title: Rest Day & Evening Nutrition Focus
today.description: Full rest day to set up a clean, consistent week of training. Focus on your evening nutrition habit: have a planned, protein-and-vegetable-rich dinner ready after work so you don't get overly hungry, and clear visible snacks from the kitchen counter. Optional 10 minutes of gentle hip flexor and hamstring stretching before bed.
alternatives: 10-15 minutes of gentle supine hamstring and hip flexor stretching before bed
today.rationale: Starting Week 2 with a scheduled rest day allows you to mentally reset after a very light previous week and focus entirely on establishing your post-work nutrition routine—having a satiating dinner ready and removing kitchen snacks—so you enter Tuesday's full 55-minute gym and rowing session energized and ready for consistent execution.

tomorrow.title: Back-Safe Gym Strength, Beginner Rowing & Hip Mobility
tomorrow.description:
Since last week's gym session was cut short at 21 minutes, today is about completing the full routine calmly with strict form.

1. Beginner Rowing Technique Warm-up (15 min): Set damper to 3–4. Focus on sequence: Legs -> Body -> Arms on the drive, then Arms -> Body -> Legs on the recovery. Row 3 x 4 minutes at 18–20 strokes per minute (spm) with 1 minute easy rest between bouts. Keep heart rate under 130 bpm.

2. Strength Circuit (30 min): Rest 60–90s between sets. Stop immediately if you feel any lower-back twinge.
- Goblet Squat: 1 warm-up set of 10 reps at 4–6 kg, then 3 x 10 reps at 12 kg (upright torso, knees tracking toes).
- Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift (RDL): 3 x 10 reps with light dumbbells (8–10 kg per hand). Keep a slight knee bend, brace your core, and hinge strictly at the hips until you feel a mild hamstring stretch (mid-shin height)—never round the lower back.
- Glute Bridges: 3 x 12 reps with a 2-second squeeze at the top.
- Lat Pulldown: 3 x 10 reps at 40–50 kg (controlled return).
- Pallof Press (Anti-Rotation Core): 3 x 10 reps per side with a 2-second hold at full extension.
- Front Plank: 3 x 30 seconds (focus on glute squeeze and ribs down).

3. Dedicated Hip & Hamstring Mobility (10 min): Do not skip this—2.5 minutes isn't enough to relieve sit-bone pressure on the bike. Do 2 rounds of: Couch stretch or half-kneeling hip flexor stretch (60s/side), 90/90 hip switches (60s), and supine hamstring strap/towel stretch with a flat lower back (60s/side).
alternatives: If the rowing machine is occupied, use a 15-minute incline treadmill walk or stair machine warm-up at HR <130 bpm before the lifting circuit.
tomorrow.rationale: Completing the full 55-minute gym session is the top structural priority of this week. By adding the third set of 12 kg goblet squats, introducing light strict-hinge RDLs, and locking in a full 10 minutes of hip/hamstring stretching alongside beginner rowing technique, we directly address your lower-back vulnerability and upright cycling posture.
tomorrow.optionalRationale: This session builds the posterior-chain resilience, core anti-rotation stability, and pelvic/hamstring mobility needed to rotate your pelvis forward on the bike—relieving sit-bone blisters and lower-back ache during the 2027 brevets and Paris-Brest-Paris. Skipping it delays your structural progression and leaves your back vulnerable on long climbs and during carpentry work.
